promptHead: Athlete goal: 5K (Corrowmore Harvest 5K) on Sun Nov 15 2026, 10 weeks out, target run the whole way.

new.headline: You made a strong start with three pain-free walk-runs. Keep to three run days next week and stretch the jogs from 1 minute to 90 seconds, at an easier effort.

flags.title: Effort on the running bits
flags.detail: Last week felt 6-7/10. Jog slowly enough to talk in full sentences, about 4-5/10. If you check your watch, keep your heart rate under about 140.

flags.title: Calf tightness
flags.detail: Tight the day after a run and gone by the next morning is fine for now. If it lasts into your next run or turns into pain, skip that run and see a physio.

flags.title: The 90-second step
flags.detail: Wednesday is your first longer jog. If it feels harder than 6/10, repeat the same session on Saturday rather than adding a round.

flags.title: Three run days
flags.detail: Wanting to do more is a good sign, but run only on Monday, Wednesday and Saturday, with dog walks in between.

answers.question: I want to be ready for the 5K in November. Should I run every day next week to get there faster?
answers.answer:
No, keep to three run days. You get fitter while you recover between runs, not during the runs themselves. The calf tightness after each run shows your legs are still adapting.

Bones and tendons adapt more slowly than heart and lungs. New runners who add days quickly often pick up niggles that cost them weeks. That would slow you down, not speed you up.

Ten weeks with three runs a week is enough time to run the whole 5K. Most beginner plans take people from walk-run to 30 minutes of non-stop running in about nine weeks on that schedule.

On the other days, keep walking the dog. That easy time on your feet helps without cutting into your recovery. The short strength session on Tuesday adds a bit more.

new.analysis:
Your first week was steady and well controlled. You ran every round at almost the same pace, your heart rate barely drifted, and you had no pain in any session.

| Day | Time | Distance | Avg HR | Effort |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Mon Aug 24 | 20 min | 2.09 km | 134 | 6/10 |
| Wed Aug 26 | 20 min | 2.09 km | 132 | 6/10 |
| Sat Aug 29 | 24 min | 2.61 km | 132 | 7/10 |

The one thing to change is how hard the running bits feel. Effort 6-7/10 on a 20-minute walk-run means the jog is a little quick for now. About a quarter of your time was in zone 3, and slowing down now will help you link the jogs together later.

Your splits suggest you ran about 1 minute and walked about 1.5 minutes each round. Next week stretches the jog to 90 seconds with a longer walk, so your total running time rises only a little. I've kept the step small on purpose, because your calves and tendons need longer to adapt than your breathing does.

You are in the build phase, but for you that means building running time, not adding hard sessions. Running the whole way comes from time on your feet at an easy effort. Fast sessions would add risk and give you nothing back at this stage.

The longer view is simple. Over the coming weeks the jogs get longer and the walks shorter, with a lighter week around Sep 14 – 20. By mid-October the aim is 20 minutes of non-stop jogging. After that we build towards about 40 minutes, which covers 5K at a gentle pace.
